A sequence `A : Seq` consists of a total map `A.map : ℕ → ℝ`, a first index `A.init : ℕ`, and an end marker `A.final : WithTop ℕ` holding one past the last index. `A.final = none` marks an infinite sequence; a finite sequence occupies the index range `[A.init, A.final)`.

The window is what lets a single type carry both finite and infinite sequences, and it is why the limit definition must explicitly require `A.final = none`: asking for the limit of a finite sequence is a category error rather than a false statement.
